It is the first half of an unstable implementation of rust-lang/rfcs#3729, adding new supertraits of `Sized` - `MetaSized` and `PointeeSized` - to `std::marker`. A quick refresher of the RFC: `MetaSized` is implemented for everything except `extern type` and is intended to correspond to those types where their size is known given pointer metadata (string slices, dyn trait, etc) - basically what `?Sized` means today. `PointeeSized` includes types whose size is unknowable and is implemented for everything including `extern type`. This allows a distinction to be drawn between `extern type` and everything else, allowing `size_of_val` and `align_of_val` to reject instantiations with `extern type`, unblocking that feature. Both names are subject to bikeshed in the RFC. ```text ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ┌─────────────────────┐ │ │ │ ┌───────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Sized │ MetaSized │ PointeeSized │ │ │ └───────┘ │ │ │ └─────────────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` This half of the RFC could feasibly be stabilised without the rest of the RFC's contents and unblocks `extern type`s.
